chunks: He who observes the shortcomings of others and disapproves of them and then accepts them for himself is definitely a fool.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a fool in Islamic ethics according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) identifies this specific type of self-deception as true folly, distinguishing it from mere ignorance by highlighting the conscious hypocrisy of judging others while excusing oneself. This concept is central to the Shia ethical tradition of *muhasaba* (self-accountability), urging believers to apply the same rigorous standards to their own souls that they apply to the faults of others. It serves as a practical guide for spiritual purification, warning that the failure to recognize one's own flaws while criticizing others is the hallmark of the 'fool' who lacks true self-awareness.
